centralFinding: TubeForge can produce visually attractive scenes, but it does not consistently produce meaningful motion. Camera movement alone must not qualify as successful animation (the VQ1 acceptance rule).

engineeringPriorities.P1: subject animation — facial expression systems, eye and mouth movement, object transformation, mechanical movement, character gestures
engineeringPriorities.P2: temporal continuity — scene-entry and exit states, persistent object identity, no unexplained character appearances, stable geometry across frames
engineeringPriorities.P3: environmental animation — water movement, smoke and particles, lighting changes, atmospheric depth, background movement
engineeringPriorities.P4: camera choreography — dolly and tracking, parallax, controlled zoom, focus changes, camera movement coordinated with subject movement
engineeringPriorities.P5: profile-specific quality control — different video types need different motion expectations (a podcast is not a mechanical explainer)

specialRequirements.islamicHistory: preserve historical scene continuity and avoid generating visible depictions of prominent religious figures where the production brief prohibits them

rebenchmarkProtocol.reviewers: three or more independent blind reviewers
rebenchmarkProtocol.fixedConditions: the same scene durations and sampling points
rebenchmarkProtocol.trigger: repeat after the VQ1 implementation rounds land
